reason: Enerstock confirms that all direct prices are shown in its mobile application and that occasional users can enter through the charger QR-code payment flow, but no anonymous public station/EVSE tariff feed, reusable guest API, or deterministic PAN FR*ENT EVSE-to-QR/app-price mapping was recovered. Current official material also documents promotional/privilege pricing at individual sites, so a national or power-band fallback would be unsafe.
pathsChecked: official iOS application listing and version history
public web/search surfaces for app/API/endpoints and FR*ENT/legacy FR*ENR identifiers
third-party station tariff surfaces as corroboration only

officialEvidence.finding: Official FAQ states that all prices are indicated in the Enerstock application; occasional charging is initiated by scanning the charger QR code and entering a payment method.
Official operator page confirms public-partner chargers use QR/NFC and may be paid or free.
Official site documents site-specific commercial actions giving Enerstock users a privileged recharge price, proving that one operator-wide price cannot be safely inferred.
Official app listing supports station-ID/QR launch and price-related restrictions/promotional tariffs, but does not expose an anonymous reusable tariff feed.

tccRule: Do not assign an Enerstock price unless an exact tariff is captured for the same station/EVSE from the official app/QR payment surface or another source that deterministically identifies that EVSE. Leave every other FR*ENT row unpriced.
